source.title: Wide-minima Density Hypothesis and the Explore-Exploit Learning Rate Schedule
source.authors: Nikhil Iyer; V. Thejas; Nipun Kwatra; R. Ramjee; Muthian Sivathanu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies learning-rate schedules and measures test accuracy, training loss, and two sharpness measures in relation to generalization. This is a conceptual test of schedule-dependent generalization and sharpness, not the claim's random-label memorization test or magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's experiments that vary explore duration or compare learning-rate schedules and report generalization or sharpness. Results cited from prior work are not included. Hyperparameter sensitivity results report accuracy and are included; schedule comparisons are included as comparators. The paper does not test the random-label claim, width beyond interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizer generalization comparisons, or example removal.
record.test_reason: The study measures learning-rate schedule effects, Keskar loss sharpness, and Fisher curvature. It does not measure V7's magnitude-aware tolerance before training error rises or compare generalization-gap rankings. No other version is tested. Related sharpness results do not justify a V7 limits_scope verdict.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors interpret their exploration and sharpness results as evidence that wide minima are rarer than narrow minima; they do not directly measure minima density. They also conclude that their Knee schedule improves performance over hand-tuned baselines at full budgets and reaches comparable performance with shorter training across their tested tasks.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies learning-rate schedule and measures generalization plus Keskar sharpness and Fisher score; V7 concerns weight-magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance and ranking of generalization gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Explore duration at the initial learning rate and at a finer learning-rate scale changes test performance and reported sharpness; total training budget changes how schedule comparisons perform; seed learning rate affects final accuracy and the optimal explore duration.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10 ResNet-18, increasing finer-scale exploration from 10 to 50 epochs raises accuracy from 94.78% to 95.10% while Keskar sharpness falls from 5.48 to 3.54; training losses remain low.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Across these learning-rate schedules, lower Keskar loss sharpness accompanies better held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing initial exploration from 0 to 100 epochs lowers mean Keskar sharpness from 10.56 to 3.54 and Fisher score from 0.051 to 0.042; accuracy distributions shift upward.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Longer high-learning-rate exploration produces lower measured loss sharpness and Fisher curvature alongside better accuracy in this setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Thirty explore epochs yield mean accuracy 94.81%, with one of 50 trials reaching 95.24%; 10,000 epochs at fixed learning rate 0.001 yield 93.9%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Exploration duration and learning-rate scale affect typical accuracy, while occasional short-exploration trials attain high accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed 50-epoch budget, increasing Transformer exploration from 5 to 40 epochs raises IWSLT test BLEU from 34.93 to 35.53 without measuring sharpness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Longer exploration improves translation performance within this tested schedule range.

fits_no_version.finding: Knee improves full-budget accuracy over step schedules and approximately matches their accuracy with shorter training: CIFAR-10 95.14% in 150 versus 95.10% in 200 epochs; ImageNet 75.92% in 50 versus 75.87% in 90 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the learning-rate schedule can improve accuracy or reduce the training budget needed to reach a target accuracy.

record.problems: The V7 measure is not tested directly: the paper uses Keskar sharpness and Fisher score, and does not compare their ability to rank generalization gaps. The central density hypothesis is inferential from schedule-dependent distributions rather than a direct density measurement. Some distribution results appear only in figures. Several experiments have small numbers of runs, though reported means and standard deviations vary by experiment.
record.rows_left_out: Capped at 60 rows. Rows R1-R8 preserve figure-only distribution conditions; R9-R60 preserve the numerical and textual results selected for V7. Other schedule comparison results across ImageNet, NLP tasks, BERT, and appendix tables are omitted after prioritizing direct explore-duration and sharpness results plus representative schedule comparisons; see Tables 5–25 and Appendix B. Some duplicated aggregate schedule comparisons in Table 5 and detailed tables are not repeated.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local-connectivity effects.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under comparable tuning.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that change their difference.
Adding or removing dropout and its interactions with data size, augmentation, and weight decay.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance before training error rises, its relation to generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Related loss-sharpness and Fisher-curvature measurements do not establish these results.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All states are cannot_determine relative to the supplied claim versions, not declarations that the reported schedule effects are absent. Using different sharpness measures is an untested part of V7, not evidence that V7 needs qualification. The study varies neither batch size nor optimizer within the relevant comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; random-label held-out chance performance.
Widening beyond zero training error and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD generalization under different tuning or weight-decay recipes.
Large versus small batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbations and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures; paper uses Keskar sharpness and Fisher score instead.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring subsequent test accuracy.
